chapters.reason: The paper focuses on training models to generate shorter, accurate reasoning paths by fine-tuning on datasets containing both complete and skipped reasoning sequences.
The approach uses iterative refinement and fine-tuning to encourage step-skipping behavior rather than relying on explicit length-penalty reward functions.
The paper introduces a controlled framework to evaluate the trade-offs between reasoning efficiency (step skipping) and accuracy, contributing to the study of reasoning efficiency metrics.
